execution_steps: 1. Surveyed safetensors's remaining capabilities after the ipynb sweep. SAFETENSORS-PRESERVE-001 was 11/12 unresolved (one obligation, __metadata__ absence-vs-empty distinction, already correctly closed in an earlier tick). 2. Read test_reference_header_layout_lazy_slice.py in full: an already-written, comprehensive test file (24 tests) whose own section comments map directly onto these obligations by content, though its inline comments cite an OLDER, now-stale set of obligation IDs from before a SAL fact rehash -- the test CONTENT was still exactly on-target, so obligations were matched by rule_text meaning, not by the stale in-file ID comments.

Found two genuine test gaps and closed them with new tests before citing anything: (a) no test proved a non-object JSON header root (array/string/number/null) is rejected -- added test_non_object_header_root_is_rejected (4 cases) to test_obligation_invalid_headers.py; (b) no test proved a BYTE-ALIGNED sub-byte tensor (e.g. F4 with an even element count) is ACCEPTED, only that a misaligned one is rejected -- added test_byte_aligned_sub_byte_tensor_is_accepted to test_reference_header_layout_lazy_slice.py, required because the reconciler's schema mandates at least one positive_test_selector for `implemented` status.
5. Ran every candidate test directly before citing any of it: 107 tests across the 8 pre-existing files plus the 5 new tests, all passed.

Rewrote source_symbols per obligation to the actual implementing function (_decode_header, _header_extent, or TensorDescriptor) instead of the generic six-symbol writer/model list, and split positive/negative test selectors precisely per obligation's specific rule_text rather than reusing one shared set.
